name: read
description: Read a text file, or several whole files at once with `paths`, as `anchor│content` rows: a 4-character anchor (letters only, case-sensitive), `│`, then the line. Target edits by anchor, never by content or line number. `offset` takes a 1-indexed line number or a served anchor; with an anchor, `limit` counts lines after it — no line-number math. Page long files with `offset` and `limit`; when output says truncated, continue from the hinted `offset`. A stale anchor is refused with the current rows and fresh anchors. Images attach visually; binary, directory, and UTF-16/UTF-32 text are rejected; an empty file returns one empty row you can replace to seed content.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

paths.description: Several files to read whole in one call, each under a `== path` header. Use instead of `path` and of `cat` in bash; edit them by the anchors served here

offset.description: Line number (1-indexed) or a served anchor to start reading from

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read from offset

name: bash
description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

anyOf.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

name: write
description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

name: replace
description:
Replace a range of lines (or a single line) in a text file by anchor: `remove_from` and `remove_to` are the 4-character anchors of its first and last line, `text` is the exact replacement text, and `replace_from`/`replace_to` are accepted as aliases. Deleting every line empties the file, and the result names the empty-line anchor, so a follow-up `replace` can seed content without a `read`.

To change only part of a line without retyping the rest, use `replace_match` instead; it preserves every character the request does not name.

remove_from.description: 4-char anchor of the FIRST line to remove.

remove_to.description: 4-char anchor of the LAST line to remove.

text.description: The exact text to write in place of the removed range. "" deletes the range. A trailing line break sets the newline of the last line written instead of adding a blank line; a lone newline writes one blank line.

name: replace_match
description:
Replace part of a line (or a range of lines) without retyping the rest. `replace_from`/`replace_to` are bare anchors from served `anchor│content` rows marking the range's first and last line (the same anchor for one line), and `old_string` is the exact text to find inside that range. Send only the smallest fragment that contains the change — never text that `new_string` leaves unchanged; for a whole-line or whole-range rewrite use `replace` with the same anchors instead. `remove_from`/`remove_to` are accepted as aliases.

The two boundary anchors must still match what was last shown; lines strictly inside the range are matched against the file as it is on disk.

replace_from.description: 4-char anchor of the FIRST line of the range searched.

replace_to.description: 4-char anchor of the LAST line of the range searched; same as replace_from for a single line.

old_string.description: The exact text to find inside the selected line(s), copied from the served row: only the fragment that changes, never text that `new_string` leaves unchanged. Every occurrence inside the range is replaced; the text around each match is left untouched. Matching uses LF line breaks and excludes the last line's terminator. For a whole-line or whole-range rewrite use `replace` with the same anchors.

new_string.description: The exact replacement for every matched occurrence. "" deletes the matches. A trailing line break sets the newline of the last line written instead of adding a blank line; a lone newline writes one blank line. The rest of the range is kept byte-for-byte.

name: insert
description: Insert text after or before one existing line, addressed by `anchor` (a bare anchor from any served `anchor│content` row). `direction` places `text` after or before the anchor line; `text` is the exact text to insert.

anchor.description: 4-char anchor of the line to insert next to.

text.description: The exact text to insert; an empty string inserts one blank line. A trailing line break sets the newline of the last line written instead of adding a blank line; a lone newline writes one blank line. Never include the anchor line.

name: copy
description:
Duplicate a range of lines at another anchor, in this or another file. The source rows and anchors stay live; the copied lines get fresh anchors in the destination's post-edit diff and keep their source line endings.

A copy duplicates the content its source anchors were served from, so a same-message edit to the source file does not change what is copied.

source_from.description: 4-char anchor of the FIRST source line to copy.

source_to.description: 4-char anchor of the LAST source line to copy.

anchor.description: 4-char anchor of the destination line; the block lands before or after it and it may live in another file.

direction.description: "after" places the block below the anchor line, "before" above it

name: move
description:
Relocate a range of lines to another anchor, in this or another file. Within one file the destination must sit outside the source range; moving a range onto itself reports `No changes made` and leaves the anchors alone.

A cross-file move commits on its own when its source file also has batched edits in the message.

source_from.description: 4-char anchor of the FIRST source line to copy.

source_to.description: 4-char anchor of the LAST source line to copy.

anchor.description: 4-char anchor of the destination line; the block lands before or after it and it may live in another file.

direction.description: "after" places the block below the anchor line, "before" above it

name: undo_last_change
description: Undo the last replace, replace_match, insert, copy, or move on a file, restoring the previous content, BOM, and line endings. If the file changed since that edit, the undo is refused and the file is left untouched; a file deleted since the edit is restored.

path.description: Path to the file to undo

name: context_tree_query
description: Retrieve original tool call results that have been pruned from active context. Pass the short refs listed in a pruner-summary message, e.g. context_tree_query({ toolCallIds: ["t12", "t3"] }), to get back the full original outputs. A raw id that was reused returns every occurrence, each labelled id@timestamp. Results include the original image blocks when the pruned output carried images.

toolCallIds.description: Required. One or more short refs (e.g. "t12") or raw tool call IDs from a pruner-summary message. A reused raw id returns every occurrence, each labelled id@timestamp.

name: todo
description: Manage a task list for tracking multi-step progress. Actions: create (new task), update (change status/fields/dependencies), list (all tasks, optionally filtered by status), get (single task details), delete (tombstone), clear (reset all). Status: pending → in_progress → completed, plus deleted tombstone. Use this to plan and track multi-step work like research, design, and implementation.

activeForm.description: Present-continuous spinner label shown while status is in_progress (e.g. 'writing tests')

status.description: Set this task's status (update): one of pending, in_progress, completed, deleted. When action is list, filters returned tasks by this status.

addBlockedBy.description: Task ids to add to blockedBy (update only, additive merge)

removeBlockedBy.description: Task ids to remove from blockedBy (update only, additive merge)

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata; pass null value for a key to delete that key on update

id.description: Task id (required for update, get, delete)

includeDeleted.description: If true, list action returns deleted (tombstoned) tasks as well. Default: false.

name: create_goal
description: Create and focus a persistent goal only on explicit user request. The agent keeps working toward it across turns until update_goal marks it complete.

objective.description: Full objective; preserve ordered steps and done criteria.

token_budget.description: Whole-token budget, only if supplied by the user.

name: get_goal
description: Read the goal: objective, status, tokens used and budget.

name: update_goal
description: Mark the goal complete once its done criteria are met, with the evidence that shows it.

evidence.description: Commands and results that prove the done criteria are met.

name: load_tools
description: Enable optional tools for agents, background terminals, or web research. Call once with the needed groups; loaded tools remain active for the session.

groups.description: Optional capabilities to enable: agents, terminals, or web.

name: subagent
description: Spawn child agents that run as separate processes with their own context and every tool except load_tools and ask_user_question. Pass {label, prompt} for one child or {tasks: [{label, prompt}, ...]} to run several in parallel. The result is each child's final answer. With background: true it returns run ids at once and each answer arrives later as a message.

label.description: Required for a single child: agent chip label (e.g. 'api reviewer')

prompt.description: Self-contained task for a single child; it does not see this conversation

model.description: Model for the child, e.g. 'claude-sonnet-5-5'. 'inherit' or omitted uses yours.

effort.description: Optional reasoning effort for the child. Omit for yours.

cwd.description: Working directory for the children (default: current working directory)

background.description: Return at once and deliver answers as messages when they finish (default: false)

name: bg_start
description: Start a long-running shell command as a background terminal (executed via sh -c). Fire-and-forget: this returns immediately with an id, and you get a message with the final output when the process exits. The process receives NO stdin (immediate EOF) and there is no way to send input later — interactive commands will not work; use bg_kill to stop a stuck one. Terminals are session-scoped: they are killed when the agent exits. Output shown to you is tail-truncated (stdout 16.0KB, stderr 8.0KB); the full logs are captured to files and in the /ps viewer. Max 8 background terminals can run at once.

command.description: Shell command line to run in the background (sh -c). It receives no stdin (EOF immediately); interactive commands will not work.

title.description: Short human-readable name shown in listings and the UI

name: bg_status
description: Peek at a background terminal's status and current output (tail-truncated) without blocking. If the terminal already exited, this returns its final state.

name: bg_list
description: List all background terminals (running and settled) with pid, elapsed time, exit status, and output sizes.

name: bg_kill
description: Stop one or more running background terminals (SIGTERM to the whole process tree, escalating to SIGKILL). Returns each terminal's final state; already-settled ids are reported as such.

name: ask_user_question
description:
Ask the user one or more structured questions during execution. Use when you need to:
1. Gather user preferences or requirements
2. Clarify ambiguous instructions
3. Get decisions on implementation choices as you work
4. Offer choices to the user about what direction to take

Usage notes:
- Users can type a custom answer via the automatically appended "Type something." row on every question or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author "Other" or "Type something." labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.
- Use multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. The "Type something." row is available on every question, including when options carry a `preview`; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column.
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: MAX 16 CHARACTERS — hard limit, requests over the limit are rejected. Very short chip/tag shown next to the question. Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

label.description: MAX 60 CHARACTERS — hard limit, requests over the limit are rejected. The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). The 'Type something.' row is appended automatically — do NOT author it.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

name: fd
description: Find files and directories by name with fd. Respects .gitignore by default. Results are limited to 1000 entries unless a higher limit is given; output is limited to 2000 lines or 50KB, and complete truncated output is saved to a temporary file.

pattern.description: Regex matched against file names (or a glob when glob is true). Omit to list everything under path.

path.description: Directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

type.description: Only return entries of this type: file, directory, or symlink.

extension.description: Only return files with this extension, e.g. 'ts' or 'md'.

glob.description: Treat pattern as a glob (e.g. '*.test.ts') instead of a regex.

hidden.description: Include hidden files and directories. Defaults to false.

limit.description: Maximum number of results (1-10000). Defaults to 1000.

name: rg
description: Search file contents with ripgrep. Uses smart-case matching, respects .gitignore by default, and returns at most 100 matches per file unless a different limit is given. Rows are `path:anchor│line` for matches and `path-anchor│line` for context; the anchors work in replace, insert and the other edit tools without a read. Output is limited to 2000 lines or 50KB; complete truncated output is saved to a temporary file.

pattern.description: Regex to search for (literal text when fixed_strings is true).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

glob.description: Only search files matching this glob, e.g. '*.ts' or 'src/**'.

file_type.description: Only search files of this ripgrep type, e.g. 'ts', 'js', 'py', 'rust'.

case_sensitive.description: true forces case-sensitive matching, false forces case-insensitive. Defaults to smart-case.

fixed_strings.description: Treat pattern as a literal string instead of a regex.

hidden.description: Search hidden files and directories. Defaults to false.

context.description: Lines of context to show around each match (0-20).

limit.description: Maximum matches per file (1-1000). Defaults to 100.
